assessment.nobel_worthiness: Random-coefficients discrete-choice demand estimation with endogenous prices (BLP) and its dynamic-industry extensions (Ericson-Pakes) made structural estimation of demand, market power and merger effects routine. The methods are used in IO, trade, health, environmental and public economics, and in antitrust practice, which makes the breadth of influence unusually large.
assessment.attribution: The BLP trio of Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes is the cleanest core, with Pakes also central to dynamic games and the Ericson-Pakes framework. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin made important complementary contributions, but a three-person limit forces exclusions and the credit is arguably wider than three.
assessment.maturity: BLP dates from 1995 and has decades of confirmed use and extension. The case is mature, and it has not yet been recognised.
uncertainties: Whether Bresnahan (earlier demand-system and market-power work) should displace Levinsohn.
How much weight to give the structural-versus-reduced-form methodological debate.
As an IO researcher I am close to this field, so I have tried to apply the same criteria as for the other fields.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal open-economy framework (the 'Redux' model and the foundations of modern international macroeconomics) put current accounts, exchange rates and welfare analysis on microfoundations. The exchange-rate disconnect and Meese-Rogoff puzzles organised decades of empirical and theoretical work, and the textbook has trained generations of researchers.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the joint authors of the central framework and the central puzzles. Credit for the exchange-rate-disconnect puzzles also extends to others such as Meese, Engel and Betts-Devereux, and the pricing-to-market literature has other contributors.
assessment.maturity: The core work dates from the 1990s and has been confirmed and extended for about three decades. Timing is ripe.
uncertainties: How much of the pricing-to-market and exchange-rate pass-through literature, which is adjacent to my own research, should count as part of this contribution rather than as separate work.
Whether the committee prefers to recognise international macroeconomics through this pair or through another combination.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The sufficient-statistics approach and the empirical elasticity-of-taxable-income literature rebuilt the empirical foundations of optimal tax and public policy design. It links theory (Mirrlees, Diamond-Saez) directly to quasi-experimental estimation. The impact on policy debates and on public economics practice is large.
assessment.attribution: Saez is central to the taxable-income and optimal-tax work, with Slemrod as an important earlier contributor on taxable income. Chetty's sufficient-statistics work is closely related, though much of his best-known work sits in other lists (mobility). Stantcheva is more recent.
assessment.maturity: Work from the late 1990s to the 2010s, with extensive replication and use. Timing is fairly mature, though Chetty and Stantcheva are mid-career.
uncertainties: Whether Slemrod should be included in preference to Chetty.
Overlap with the inequality (B050) and mobility (B038) candidacies makes the allocation of credit across lists unclear.
Robustness of high-income elasticity estimates is debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed how trade economists think about the gains from trade, reallocation and the margins of adjustment. It has been supported by a large body of firm-level evidence and extended to FDI, offshoring and welfare measurement.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the core model. Helpman contributed the firm-level trade and FDI work (Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple) and earlier foundations in monopolistic-competition trade theory. Redding has significant quantitative extensions, while Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum and Bernard-Jensen provided key empirical and early heterogeneous-firm foundations, so credit is contestable.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation. The Krugman prize (2008) covered the earlier new trade theory, so this is a plausible follow-on.
uncertainties: Attribution among Melitz, Eaton-Kortum, Bernard et al. and Helpman is unsettled, and a three-person limit may exclude important contributors.
I work in trade and industrial organisation, so I try not to favour this candidate on field proximity alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Staggered pricing, the Taylor rule and the microfounded New Keynesian framework underpin the modern analysis of monetary policy and inflation targeting at central banks. This is one of the most influential bodies of work in applied macroeconomics.
assessment.attribution: The credit is highly dispersed across Calvo (time-dependent pricing), Taylor (contracts and the rule), Woodford (the policy framework), Gali, Gertler, Clarida, Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans and Smets-Wouters. Any three-person selection leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the 1980s to the early 2000s and has been tested through several decades of policy use, including the post-2008 and post-2020 inflation episodes.
uncertainties: The allocation of credit among many contributors is hard.
Empirical performance of the framework in the 2021-23 inflation is debated.
The ranking is sensitive to the choice of trio. Hassler, the chair, is a co-author on my own menu-cost paper, which is nominal-rigidity-adjacent. I note this as a disclosure only.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The China-shock studies and the task-based analysis of technology reshaped understanding of how trade and automation affect local labour markets and inequality. The work is highly policy-relevant and bridges labour and trade economics.
assessment.attribution: The China-shock work is Autor-Dorn-Hanson. The task-based framework and the skill-biased technical change work involve Katz, Acemoglu and Autor-Levy-Murnane. Credit for the technology strand is more diffuse than for the trade-shock strand.
assessment.maturity: The China-shock results date from 2013 onward and are well replicated, though the long-run interpretation is still contested, so timing is somewhat less mature than for the top candidates.
uncertainties: The long-run persistence and magnitude of the effects are debated.
Overlap with the Acemoglu-Johnson-Robinson and Goldin recognitions needs weighing.
Whether the trade-shock and technology strands should be treated as a single contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators (Arellano-Bond, Arellano-Bover, Blundell-Bond) are among the most widely used tools in applied economics, especially in growth, finance, IO and labour. The methodological contribution is widely used but is incremental relative to the Nobel-recognised econometric advances.
assessment.attribution: The three credited names are the standard attribution for the main estimators. Anderson-Hsiao, Holtz-Eakin-Newey-Rosen and Hansen's GMM are also important antecedents, and Hansen's GMM is already recognised.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from 1991 to 1998 and has been confirmed by extensive use, though the weak-instrument and proliferation problems are known.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the work as a sufficiently original conceptual advance rather than a refinement of GMM.
Blundell's other contributions (B033) overlap, so credit could be allocated differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification and bounds changed how researchers think about what can be learned from data under credible assumptions. Manski's work on the reflection problem, selection and treatment-response bounds is foundational, and the moment-inequality methods (Tamer and Molinari among others) made it empirically operational.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clear originator. Tamer and Molinari developed key inferential and econometric extensions, and Chernozhukov-Hong-Tamer and Imbens-Manski are related contributions. Credit beyond Manski is somewhat diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Manski's foundational work dates from the late 1980s and 1990s. The moment-inequality extensions are from the 2000s and 2010s, so the foundation is well confirmed while parts of the practice are still maturing.
uncertainties: Applied uptake is narrower than for estimators such as GMM or difference-in-differences.
Whether the committee would prefer to recognise Manski alone or with later contributors.
The field-balance considerations across many econometrics candidates (B010, B021, B023, B034, B043) remain open.
